Definition: Recursively eliminates the least important features based on model importance.
Pros: Tends to give better results, handles multicollinearity well.
Cons: Computationally expensive, especially with many features.

Definition: Starts with an empty model and adds features one by one, selecting the feature that improves the model the most.
Pros: Less computationally expensive, easy to implement.
Cons: Can miss feature interactions, less effective with multicollinearity.

Definition: Starts with all features and removes them one by one, selecting the feature that, when removed, improves the model the most.
Pros: Captures feature interactions better, useful with smaller initial feature sets.
Cons: Computationally expensive, can overfit if not carefully managed.

Definition: Selects the top K features based on a specified statistical test.
Cons: Does not consider feature interactions, only considers individual feature relevance.

Definition: Uses feature importance scores from a Random Forest model to select the most relevant features.
Pros: Captures feature interactions and non-linear relationships, robust to overfitting.
Cons: Computationally expensive, requires tuning of Random Forest hyperparameters.

Definition: Selects a percentage of the best features based on a specified statistical test.
Pros: Simple, fast, computationally efficient, allows for flexible selection of features.
Cons: Does not consider feature interactions, only considers individual feature relevance.
